data.name: Avishal
data.gender_notes: Avishal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Avishal is a Sanskrit and Hindi name meaning 'Lord of Peace'. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'avishala', which means 'immutable', 'unshaken', 'unconquerable'. It is a powerful name that evokes a sense of calmness, stability, and strength. The name Avishal carries the meaning “Lord of Peace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Avishal usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of peace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Avishal is a name that resonates with the divine energy of the Hindu deity Agni, the god of fire. It represents the power and strength of the universe and the inner peace and tranquility that comes from connecting with that power.
data.etymology: Avishal belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Peace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avishal total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Avishal represents the eternal and divine qualities of peace and stability. In Hindu culture, peace is a highly revered value, and is often sought after through various spiritual practices, such as meditation and self-discipline. By giving a child the name Avishal, parents are imbuing him or her with the qualities of peace, tranquility, and resilience, which are valuable traits in the tumultuous world. This name is also significant during times of turmoil or crisis, as it serves as a reminder of the perfect peace that can be found within oneself, despite external circumstances.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Avishal signifies the unshakable inner peace that comes from a deep connection with the divine. As the name suggests, an Avishal person is untouched by the external disturbances and is firmly anchored in inner calmness. This name is particularly significant for spiritual seekers, as it encourages the cultivation of inner peace and stability, which are essential for spiritual growth and self-realization. It serves as a constant reminder of the ultimate reality, which is beyond the transient and ever-changing physical world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Avishal: Radiant Peace. A name that signifies the inner tranquility and serenity, shining brightly from within.

historical_references.reference: Avishala was the name of a king in ancient India, who ruled over the Vatsa kingdom in the 5th century BCE. He is mentioned in the Buddhist texts, particularly in the Jataka tales, as a just and generous ruler, who was revered by his people.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Buddhist texts, Vatsa kingdom, just and generous ruler

historical_references.reference: Avishaka was a minister in the court of the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. He is mentioned in various inscriptions and edicts of Ashoka, as a trusted advisor and a military commander. He is also credited with the establishment of the Sanchi Stupa, one of the oldest stone structures in India, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
